subproblem.title: The cone identity in terms of test forms (parent step 2)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) a cone current (IsConeCurrent C: for every λ > 0 and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), currentEval (blowUp C 0 λ) ω = C(ω), where blowUp C 0 λ = η_{0,λ#}C is the proper affine push-forward of C by η(y) = −λ^{-1}·0 + λ^{-1}y). Then for every λ > 0 and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) there is a test form ω' ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with ω'(y) = λ^{-n}·ω(λ^{-1}y) for every y ∈ ℝ^P and C(ω') = C(ω).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsConeCurrent C → ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, ∃ ω' : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, (∀ y, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (lam⁻¹ • y)) ∧ C ω' = C ω
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 2 ("By the contract, blowUp C 0 λ is the push-forward of C by the proper affine map η(y) = −λ^{-1}·0 + λ^{-1}y = S(y), acting by (blowUp C 0 λ)(ω) = C(η^#ω) with (η^#ω)(y) = ω(S(y))∘(λ^{-1}id) = λ^{-n}ω(λ^{-1}y) (affinePullbackForm with L = λ^{-1}id, b = 0); η^#ω is again a test form because η is a proper affine isomorphism. The domain of blowUp C 0 λ is dilation 0 λ '' univ = univ, so every test form ω on ℝ^P satisfies the test-form condition in currentEval, and IsConeCurrent C gives (2.1) C(ω) = C(η^#ω)"). Book: Simon 7.3.1(2) (cone: η_{0,λ#}C = C) and Ch. 6, 2.23 (chapter-06.txt line 408: f_#T(ω) = T(f^#ω)); the cone property is used in the proof of 7.4.5 (chapter-07.txt lines 697–698).

Fix λ > 0 and ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n. Put L := dilationCLM P λ = λ^{-1} · id (a continuous linear map of ℝ^P) and b := −(λ^{-1} · 0), so that dilation 0 λ y = b + L y for all y (definition of dilation), and put V := dilation 0 λ '' univ, the domain of blowUp C 0 λ.

1. IsConeCurrent C, applied to λ, the proof of 0 < λ, and ω, gives currentEval (blowUp C 0 λ) ω = C(ω).

2. V = ℝ^P: every x ∈ ℝ^P equals dilation 0 λ (λx), because −(λ^{-1}·0) + λ^{-1}(λx) = 0 + x = x (λ ≠ 0). Hence tsupport ω ⊆ V. Moreover ω is a test form (smooth with compact support; first component of ω.property). So the condition h : IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V in the definition of currentEval holds, the 'if' takes its positive branch, and currentEval (blowUp C 0 λ) ω = (blowUp C 0 λ) ⟨ω, h⟩.

3. By the contract's definition, blowUp C 0 λ = (C.restrictDomain h_sub).affinePushforward L b h_proper, where h_sub is the inclusion (y ↦ b + L y)^{-1}(V) ⊆ univ and h_proper the properness of y ↦ b + Ly (both proved inside the definition of blowUp). By GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply and GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply (both hold by rfl),
 (blowUp C 0 λ) ⟨ω, h⟩ = C(ω'), where ω' := testFormOnInclusion h_sub n (affinePullbackTestOn L b h_proper V n ⟨ω, h⟩).
 Here ω' is an element of TestFormOn univ n (the SimonGMT constructions affinePullbackTestOn and testFormOnInclusion produce test forms; properness of the affine map is what makes the pulled-back form compactly supported), and its underlying form is (testFormOnInclusion_coe, affinePullbackTestOn_coe, definition of affinePullbackForm)
 ω'(y) = affinePullbackForm L b ω y = (ω(b + L y)).compContinuousLinearMap L for every y ∈ ℝ^P.

4. Combining steps 1–3: C(ω') = (blowUp C 0 λ)⟨ω, h⟩ = currentEval (blowUp C 0 λ) ω = C(ω).

5. Pointwise formula. For every y, b + L y = −(λ^{-1}·0) + λ^{-1}y = λ^{-1}y. Let α := ω(λ^{-1}y), an n-covector, i.e. a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ. For v = (v_1, …, v_n) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n,
 (α.compContinuousLinearMap L)(v) = α(λ^{-1}v_1, …, λ^{-1}v_n) = (∏_{i ∈ Fin n} λ^{-1}) · α(v) = (λ^{-1})^n · α(v),
 by multilinearity (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ: f(c_1v_1, …, c_nv_n) = (∏_i c_i) · f(v); the product over Fin n of the constant λ^{-1} is (λ^{-1})^n by Finset.prod_const and card (Fin n) = n). By extensionality in v, α.compContinuousLinearMap L = (λ^{-1})^n • α. Hence ω'(y) = (λ^{-1})^n • ω(λ^{-1} • y) for every y ∈ ℝ^P.

6. By steps 3–5, ω' ∈ TestFormOn univ n satisfies ω'(y) = (λ^{-1})^n • ω(λ^{-1} • y) for all y and C(ω') = C(ω), which is the claim.
proof_key_steps: IsConeCurrent gives currentEval (blowUp C 0 λ) ω = C ω.
dilation 0 λ '' univ = univ, so currentEval takes its test-form branch.
Unfolding blowUp (affinePushforward of restrictDomain) gives C ω' for the test form ω' = affinePullbackForm (λ^{-1}·id) (−λ^{-1}·0) ω.
Multilinearity: α ∘ (λ^{-1}·id) = λ^{-n}α, so ω'(y) = λ^{-n}ω(λ^{-1}y).

audit.reason: The proposition includes every required hypothesis and matches the prose. Surjectivity makes currentEval take its test-form branch; affine push-forward and domain restriction produce the required test form. Multilinearity yields the inverse nth-power factor, including n = 0. The cone identity gives the stated evaluation equality directly.

subproblem.title: Change of variables for H^n under a dilation (parent step 1, formula (1.1))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, c > 0, T : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, T(x) = cx, H^n = μHE[n] the normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P, and M ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set (so T^{-1}(M) = {z : cz ∈ M} = c^{-1}M). Then (i) T_#(H^n⌞T^{-1}(M)) = c^{-n}·(H^n⌞M) as measures on ℝ^P (scalar ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n})); (ii) for every g : ℝ^P → [0,∞] (no measurability assumed), ∫⁻_{T^{-1}(M)} g(cz) dH^n(z) = c^{-n}·∫⁻_M g dH^n; (iii) for every g : ℝ^P → ℝ (no integrability assumed; Bochner integrals, with value 0 for non-integrable functions), ∫_{T^{-1}(M)} g(cz) dH^n(z) = c^{-n}·∫_M g dH^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → ∀ M : Set (Euclid P), Measure.map (fun x : Euclid P => c • x) (μHE[n].restrict ((fun x => c • x) ⁻¹' M)) = ENNReal.ofReal (c⁻¹ ^ n) • μHE[n].restrict M ∧ (∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ z in (fun x => c • x) ⁻¹' M, g (c • z) ∂μHE[n] = ENNReal.ofReal (c⁻¹ ^ n) * ∫⁻ y in M, g y ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ z in (fun x => c • x) ⁻¹' M, g (c • z) ∂μHE[n] = c⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ y in M, g y ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1 ("Scaling of H^n … (1.1) ∫_{S(M)} F dH^n = λ^{-n} ∫_M F(S(y)) dH^n(y), using the change of variables formula for the measurable embedding S (Mathlib integral_map_equiv / lintegral_map_equiv) and linearity in the measure"), stated for c = λ and T := S^{-1}, so that T^{-1}(M) = S(M) = c^{-1}M and F(z) = g(cz).

Notation: T(x) := cx on ℝ^P, H^n := μHE[n], and for a measure ν and a set E, ν⌞E := ν.restrict E. Throughout, c > 0, so c ≠ 0 and c^{-1} > 0.

1. T is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P (its inverse is x ↦ c^{-1}x), hence a measurable embedding for the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (Mathlib: (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero c hc).measurableEmbedding); in particular T is measurable and injective.

2. Push-forward of H^n by T. Let B ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel. Then (T_#H^n)(B) = H^n(T^{-1}(B)) (Measure.map_apply, T measurable, B measurable), and T^{-1}(B) = {x : cx ∈ B} = c^{-1}B := {c^{-1}b : b ∈ B} (Set.preimage_smul₀). The scaling law of Hausdorff measure holds for every set S and every r ≠ 0: H^n(rS) = ‖r‖₊^n · H^n(S) (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). With r = c^{-1}: H^n(c^{-1}B) = ‖c^{-1}‖₊^n · H^n(B). Since c^{-1} > 0 we have ‖c^{-1}‖₊ = c^{-1} as a nonnegative real, so the factor ‖c^{-1}‖₊^n, viewed in [0,∞], equals ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) (c^{-n} ≥ 0). Hence (T_#H^n)(B) = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · H^n(B) for every Borel B, and since two measures that agree on all measurable sets are equal, T_#H^n = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · H^n.

3. Proof of (i). For a measurable embedding T, a measure ν and an arbitrary set M (no measurability of M is needed), (T_#ν)⌞M = T_#(ν⌞T^{-1}(M)) (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map). With ν = H^n and step 2:
 T_#(H^n⌞T^{-1}(M)) = (T_#H^n)⌞M = (ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · H^n)⌞M = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · (H^n⌞M)
 (restriction commutes with scalar multiplication of the measure, Measure.restrict_smul).

4. Proof of (ii). For a measurable embedding T, a measure ν and every function g : ℝ^P → [0,∞] (measurable or not), ∫⁻ g d(T_#ν) = ∫⁻ (g ∘ T) dν (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map). Take ν = H^n⌞T^{-1}(M). Then
 ∫⁻_{T^{-1}(M)} g(cz) dH^n(z) = ∫⁻ g d(T_#(H^n⌞T^{-1}(M))) = ∫⁻ g d(ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · H^n⌞M) = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · ∫⁻_M g dH^n,
 by (i) and the linearity of the lower integral in the measure, ∫⁻ g d(a·μ) = a · ∫⁻ g dμ (lintegral_smul_measure).

5. Proof of (iii). For a measurable embedding T, a measure ν and every g : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ g d(T_#ν) = ∫ (g ∘ T) dν (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map; no integrability assumption is needed: g is T_#ν-integrable iff g ∘ T is ν-integrable, and both Bochner integrals are 0 otherwise). With ν = H^n⌞T^{-1}(M), (i), and ∫ g d(a·μ) = a.toReal · ∫ g dμ for a ∈ [0,∞] (integral_smul_measure):
 ∫_{T^{-1}(M)} g(cz) dH^n(z) = ∫ g d(ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · H^n⌞M) = (ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n})).toReal · ∫_M g dH^n = c^{-n} · ∫_M g dH^n,
 because c^{-n} ≥ 0 gives (ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n})).toReal = c^{-n} (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). This completes the proof of (i), (ii) and (iii).
proof_key_steps: T(x) = cx is a homeomorphism, hence a measurable embedding of ℝ^P.
T^{-1}(B) = c^{-1}B and the Hausdorff scaling law H^n(c^{-1}B) = c^{-n}H^n(B) give T_#H^n = c^{-n}H^n.
Restriction along the measurable embedding: T_#(H^n⌞T^{-1}M) = (T_#H^n)⌞M = c^{-n}H^n⌞M (proves (i)).
Change of variables for lower and Bochner integrals over T_#ν, plus linearity in the measure, give (ii) and (iii).

The pinned measurable-embedding restriction and integral lemmas genuinely require neither measurable M nor measurable/integrable g. All three conclusions follow without circularity.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes are invariant under dilation (parent step 3, orientation bullet)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, c > 0, z ∈ ℝ^P and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P. If Q is an approximate tangent space of M at cz in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (cz) Q: finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{cz,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0⁺, where η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x)), then Q is an approximate tangent space of {x : cx ∈ M} = c^{-1}M at z.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (c : ℝ) (z : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < c → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (c • z) Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n ((fun x => c • x) ⁻¹' M) z Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 3, orientation bullet ("For r > 0, blowUpMap z r '' M' = {r^{-1}(λ^{-1}m − z) : m ∈ M} = {(λr)^{-1}(m − λz) : m ∈ M} = blowUpMap y (λr) '' M, and λr → 0⁺ as r → 0⁺; hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' z Q"), with λ = c, y = cz and M' = λ^{-1}M = T^{-1}(M), T(x) := cx. Book: Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (chapter-03.txt line 77), approximate tangent spaces defined by blow-ups η_{x,λ}.

Recall the definition (SimonGMT Chapter03, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4): HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n E x Q means finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), the function r ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} f dH^n (integral over the image set η_{x,r}(E) with respect to H^n = μHE[n]) tends to ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0 within (0, ∞), where η_{x,r}(y) := r^{-1}(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r y). Write M' := T^{-1}(M) = {x : cx ∈ M}.

1. Dimension. finrank Q = n is the first component of the hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (cz) Q.

2. Set identity: for every r ∈ ℝ, η_{z,r}(M') = η_{cz,cr}(M).
 First, for every m ∈ ℝ^P: (cr)^{-1}(m − cz) = (r^{-1}c^{-1})(m − cz) = r^{-1}(c^{-1}m − c^{-1}(cz)) = r^{-1}(c^{-1}m − z), using (cr)^{-1} = r^{-1}c^{-1} (mul_inv_rev; this holds for all real r and c with the convention 0^{-1} = 0 of the real inverse used in the definition of η, and only r > 0 matters for the limit in step 4), (ab)•v = a•(b•v), linearity of v ↦ c^{-1}v, and c^{-1}(cz) = z (c ≠ 0).
 (⊆) Let y = η_{z,r}(m') with m' ∈ M', i.e. cm' ∈ M. Put m := cm' ∈ M. By the identity, η_{cz,cr}(m) = r^{-1}(c^{-1}(cm') − z) = r^{-1}(m' − z) = y.
 (⊇) Let y = η_{cz,cr}(m) with m ∈ M. Put m' := c^{-1}m. Then cm' = c(c^{-1}m) = m ∈ M, so m' ∈ M', and by the identity η_{z,r}(m') = r^{-1}(c^{-1}m − z) = η_{cz,cr}(m) = y.

3. The map φ(r) := cr tends to 0 within (0, ∞) as r → 0 within (0, ∞): φ is continuous with φ(0) = c·0 = 0, so φ(r) → 0 as r → 0 (in particular along r → 0⁺), and φ(r) = cr > 0 whenever r > 0 because c > 0; a function converging to 0 that eventually takes values in (0, ∞) converges within (0, ∞) (tendsto_nhdsWithin_of_tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_within).

4. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) and put F(s) := ∫_{η_{cz,s}(M)} f dH^n. By the hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (cz) Q, F(s) → ∫_Q f dH^n as s → 0⁺. By step 2, ∫_{η_{z,r}(M')} f dH^n = F(cr) = (F ∘ φ)(r) for every r. By step 3 and the composition of limits, F(φ(r)) → ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0⁺. Hence r ↦ ∫_{η_{z,r}(M')} f dH^n tends to ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0⁺.

5. Steps 1 and 4 are the two components of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' z Q, i.e. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n ((x ↦ cx)^{-1}(M)) z Q.
proof_key_steps: finrank Q = n is inherited from the hypothesis.
Set identity η_{z,r}(c^{-1}M) = η_{cz,cr}(M) for every r, from (cr)^{-1}(m − cz) = r^{-1}(c^{-1}m − z).
r ↦ cr tends to 0 within (0,∞) as r → 0⁺ because c > 0.
Compose the hypothesis limit at cz with r ↦ cr.

audit.reason: The statement matches the literal approximate-tangent predicate. The proof preserves dimension, establishes the blow-up image identity, and composes the hypothesis limit with r ↦ cr. Positivity ensures convergence within the positive half-line. No rectifiability or additional measure hypothesis is needed.

subproblem.title: Action and weight of the dilated triple (parent steps 4 and 6)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, c > 0, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) and R' be IMRep univ n triples with R'.carrier = {x : cx ∈ M}, R'.mult x = θ(cx) and R'.orient x = ξ(cx) for all x. Then (1) for every n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ^n(ℝ^P) (no regularity assumed), τ(R')(ω) = τ(R)(ω_c), where ω_c(y) := c^{-n}·ω(c^{-1}y) and τ(R)(ω) = ∫_M θ·⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n is IMRep.action; (2) for every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P, μ_{R'}(A) = c^{-n}·μ_R(cA), where μ_R = θH^n⌞M is IMRep.measure and cA = {ca : a ∈ A}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (R R' : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → R'.carrier = (fun x => c • x) ⁻¹' R.carrier → (∀ x, R'.mult x = R.mult (c • x)) → (∀ x, R'.orient x = R.orient (c • x)) → (∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, R'.action ω = R.action (fun y => (c⁻¹ ^ n) • ω (c⁻¹ • y))) ∧ ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R'.measure A = ENNReal.ofReal (c⁻¹ ^ n) * R.measure ((fun x => c • x) '' A)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 4 ("R_λ.action(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ(λz) ξ(λz)(ω(z)) dH^n(z) = λ^{-n} ∫_M θ(y) ξ(y)(ω(λ^{-1}y)) dH^n(y) = ∫_M θ(y) ξ(y)(λ^{-n}ω(λ^{-1}y)) dH^n(y) = R.action(η^#ω)", by (1.1) and linearity of ξ(y)) and step 6 ("For measurable A, M' ∩ A = S(M ∩ λA), so by (1.1) R_λ.measure(A) = ∫_{M'∩A} θ' dH^n = λ^{-n}∫_{M∩λA} θ dH^n = λ^{-n}·R.measure(λA)"), with λ = c. Uses the sibling child dilation_change_of_variables, cited as (CV)(ii) and (CV)(iii).

Notation: M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, H^n := μHE[n], T(x) := cx (c > 0, so T is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse x ↦ c^{-1}x, hence an injective measurable embedding). By hypothesis M' := R'.carrier = T^{-1}(M), R'.mult z = θ(cz) and R'.orient z = ξ(cz) for all z. Recall the definitions R.action ω = ∫_{R.carrier} (R.mult x : ℝ) · R.orient x (ω x) dH^n(x) (Bochner integral) and R.measure = (H^n⌞R.carrier).withDensity (x ↦ (R.mult x : [0,∞])).

1. Action, change of variables. Fix an arbitrary ω : ℝ^P → Λ^n(ℝ^P) (a DifferentialForm; no regularity or integrability is needed). By the definition of action and the hypotheses on R',
 R'.action ω = ∫_{T^{-1}(M)} θ(cz) · ξ(cz)(ω(z)) dH^n(z).
 Define g : ℝ^P → ℝ by g(y) := θ(y) · ξ(y)(ω(c^{-1}y)). Since c^{-1}(cz) = z, g(cz) = θ(cz) · ξ(cz)(ω(z)) for every z. By (CV)(iii) (valid for every real-valued function):
 R'.action ω = ∫_{T^{-1}(M)} g(cz) dH^n(z) = c^{-n} · ∫_M g dH^n.

2. Action, linearity. A constant factor moves inside a Bochner integral for every integrand (∫ a·f dμ = a·∫ f dμ, integral_const_mul), so c^{-n} ∫_M g dH^n = ∫_M c^{-n} · θ(y) · ξ(y)(ω(c^{-1}y)) dH^n(y). Since ξ(y) is a (continuous) linear map, ξ(y)(c^{-n} · ω(c^{-1}y)) = c^{-n} · ξ(y)(ω(c^{-1}y)) (map_smul), so for every y the integrand equals θ(y) · ξ(y)(c^{-n} · ω(c^{-1}y)) (commutativity of real multiplication). Therefore
 R'.action ω = ∫_M θ(y) · ξ(y)((c^{-1})^n • ω(c^{-1} • y)) dH^n(y) = R.action (y ↦ (c^{-1})^n • ω(c^{-1} • y)),
 by the definition of R.action. This proves the first conjunct.

3. Weight, reduction to a set integral. Fix a Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P. Its image T(A) = (x ↦ cx) '' A is Borel, because T is a measurable embedding (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image). By the definition of R'.measure and withDensity_apply on the measurable set A,
 R'.measure(A) = ∫⁻_A θ(cz) d(H^n⌞M')(z) = ∫⁻_{A ∩ M'} θ(cz) dH^n(z),
 using (H^n⌞M')⌞A = H^n⌞(A ∩ M') for measurable A (Measure.restrict_restrict). Since T is injective, z ∈ A ⇔ cz ∈ T(A); hence A ∩ M' = T^{-1}(T(A)) ∩ T^{-1}(M) = T^{-1}(T(A) ∩ M) (preimage_image_eq, preimage_inter).

4. Weight, change of variables. By (CV)(ii) applied to the set T(A) ∩ M and the function g(y) := θ(y) ∈ [0,∞]:
 ∫⁻_{T^{-1}(T(A)∩M)} θ(cz) dH^n(z) = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · ∫⁻_{T(A)∩M} θ dH^n.
 By withDensity_apply on the measurable set T(A) and Measure.restrict_restrict again, ∫⁻_{T(A)∩M} θ dH^n = ∫⁻_{T(A)} θ d(H^n⌞M) = R.measure(T(A)). Combining with step 3,
 R'.measure(A) = ENNReal.ofReal((c^{-1})^n) · R.measure((x ↦ c • x) '' A),
 which is the second conjunct.
proof_key_steps: Write R'.action ω = ∫_{T^{-1}M} g(cz) dH^n with g(y) = θ(y)ξ(y)(ω(c^{-1}y)) and apply the Bochner change of variables (sibling).
Move c^{-n} inside the integral and use linearity of ξ(y) to obtain R.action(y ↦ c^{-n}ω(c^{-1}y)).
For Borel A: R'.measure A = ∫⁻_{A∩M'} θ(c·) dH^n and A ∩ M' = T^{-1}(cA ∩ M).
The lower-integral change of variables (sibling) gives c^{-n}·R.measure(cA).

audit.reason: Both conclusions match the exact type. The action computation is valid for arbitrary forms under total Bochner integration. For measurable A, its dilation is measurable and the preimage/intersection identity gives the weight formula through withDensity and lower-integral change of variables. Only the declared dependency is required; infinite measures cause no gap.

subproblem.title: Dilating an integer multiplicity triple gives an integer multiplicity triple (parent step 3)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n: M Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable with θ > 0 on M and ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K, ξ a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞M and, for H^n⌞M-a.e. x, a unit orientation (IsUnitOrientationOf) of some approximate tangent space Q of M at x). Let c > 0. Then there is an IMRep univ n triple R' with R'.carrier = {x : cx ∈ M}, R'.mult x = θ(cx) and R'.orient x = ξ(cx) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → ∃ R' : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, R'.carrier = (fun x => c • x) ⁻¹' R.carrier ∧ (∀ x, R'.mult x = R.mult (c • x)) ∧ ∀ x, R'.orient x = R.orient (c • x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 3 ("The rescaled triple R_λ := (M', θ', ξ') with M' := S(M) = λ^{-1}M, θ'(z) := θ(λz), ξ'(z) := ξ(λz) is an IMRep univ n", with its six bullets), with λ = c; note λ^{-1}M = S(M) = T^{-1}(M) for T(x) := cx. Uses the sibling children dilation_change_of_variables, cited as (CV)(i) and (CV)(ii), and tangent_space_dilation, cited as (TS). Book: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 of integer multiplicity currents (chapter-06.txt §3) and the push-forward under the homothety (Ch. 6, 2.23, chapter-06.txt line 408).

Notation: M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, T(x) := cx, M' := T^{-1}(M) = {x : cx ∈ M}, θ' := θ ∘ T, ξ' := ξ ∘ T, H^n := μHE[n], ν := H^n⌞M and ν' := H^n⌞M' (⌞ = restriction). T is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P (inverse x ↦ c^{-1}x, c ≠ 0), so it is continuous, measurable, injective and a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero c hc). By (CV)(i) applied to the set M:
 (∗) T_#ν' = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · ν.
We define R' := (M', θ', ξ') and verify the fields of IMRep univ n one by one (steps 1–8); the three identities R'.carrier = T^{-1}(M), R'.mult x = θ(cx) and R'.orient x = ξ(cx) (all x) then hold by construction (step 9).

1. measurableSet_carrier. M' = T^{-1}(M) is Borel, being the preimage of the Borel set M (R.measurableSet_carrier) under the measurable map T.

2. carrier_subset. M' ⊆ ℝ^P = univ trivially.

3. rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable n M'). By R.rectifiable there are M₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with H^n(M₀) = 0 and maps F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ), each F_j Lipschitz with some constant K_j ≥ 0, such that M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n). Put M₀' := T^{-1}(M₀) and F_j'(w) := c^{-1}F_j(w).
 (a) H^n(M₀') = 0: by (CV)(i) applied to the set M₀, T_#(H^n⌞T^{-1}(M₀)) = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · (H^n⌞M₀). Evaluate both measures on the Borel set ℝ^P: the left side gives (H^n⌞T^{-1}(M₀))(T^{-1}(ℝ^P)) = H^n(T^{-1}(M₀)), the right side ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · H^n(M₀) = 0. Hence H^n(M₀') = 0.
 (b) F_j' is Lipschitz with constant ‖c^{-1}‖₊ · K_j: it is the composition of F_j with the ‖c^{-1}‖₊-Lipschitz map x ↦ c^{-1}x (lipschitzWith_smul, LipschitzWith.comp).
 (c) Covering. Let z ∈ M'. Then cz ∈ M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n). If cz ∈ M₀ then z ∈ T^{-1}(M₀) = M₀'. Otherwise cz = F_j(w) for some j ∈ ℕ and w ∈ ℝ^n, and then z = c^{-1}(cz) = c^{-1}F_j(w) = F_j'(w) ∈ F_j'(ℝ^n). Hence M' ⊆ M₀' ∪ ⋃_j F_j'(ℝ^n).
 By (a)–(c), M' is countably n-rectifiable.

4. measurable_mult. θ' = θ ∘ T is measurable as the composition of the measurable θ (R.measurable_mult) with the measurable T.

5. mult_pos. If z ∈ M' then cz ∈ M, hence θ'(z) = θ(cz) > 0 by R.mult_pos.

6. locallyIntegrable_mult. Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact (K ⊆ univ). Then T(K) = cK is compact (continuous image of a compact set) and T(K) ⊆ univ. Since T is injective, z ∈ K ⇔ cz ∈ T(K), so
 M' ∩ K = T^{-1}(M) ∩ T^{-1}(T(K)) = T^{-1}(M ∩ T(K)).
 By (CV)(ii) applied to the set M ∩ T(K) and the function g(y) := θ(y) ∈ [0,∞]:
 ∫⁻_{M'∩K} θ'(z) dH^n(z) = ∫⁻_{T^{-1}(M∩T(K))} θ(cz) dH^n(z) = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · ∫⁻_{M∩T(K)} θ dH^n.
 The last lower integral is finite by R.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set T(K) ⊆ univ, and ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) < ∞; the product of two finite elements of [0,∞] is finite (ENNReal.mul_ne_top). So ∫⁻_{M'∩K} θ' dH^n ≠ ∞.

7. aestronglyMeasurable_orient. ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for ν (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), hence also for the scalar multiple ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · ν (every null set of ν is null for a scalar multiple of ν; AEStronglyMeasurable.smul_measure), i.e., by (∗), for T_#ν'. Since T is measurable, hence a.e.-measurable for ν', the composition ξ' = ξ ∘ T is a.e.-strongly measurable for ν' (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_aemeasurable: if g is a.e.-strongly measurable for f_#μ and f is a.e.-measurable for μ, then g ∘ f is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ).

8. orients. For y ∈ ℝ^P let p(y) be the statement: there is a linear subspace Q of ℝ^P with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q. By R.orients, p(y) holds for ν-a.e. y. A property holding ν-a.e. holds (ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · ν)-a.e. (Measure.ae_smul_measure), i.e., by (∗), T_#ν'-a.e. Because T is a measurable embedding, a property holds T_#ν'-a.e. if and only if its composition with T holds ν'-a.e. (MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff; no measurability of the property is required). Hence p(cz) holds for ν'-a.e. z. Fix such a z and Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (cz) Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(cz)) Q. By (TS) (applied to the set M, c > 0, the point z and Q), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' z Q; and ξ'(z) = ξ(cz), so IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'(z)) Q. Thus, for ν'-a.e. z, there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' z Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'(z)) Q, which is the field orients of R'.

9. Steps 1–8 supply every field of the structure IMRep univ n for the data (M', θ', ξ'); call the resulting triple R'. By construction R'.carrier = M' = (x ↦ cx)^{-1}(R.carrier), R'.mult x = θ(cx) = R.mult (c • x) and R'.orient x = ξ(cx) = R.orient (c • x) for every x, which proves the claim.
proof_key_steps: T(x) = cx is a measurable embedding with T_#(H^n⌞T^{-1}M) = c^{-n}H^n⌞M (sibling dilation_change_of_variables).
Borel carrier, positivity and measurability of θ∘T transfer directly; rectifiability via the null set T^{-1}M₀ (change of variables at univ) and the Lipschitz maps c^{-1}F_j.
Local integrability: M' ∩ K = T^{-1}(M ∩ cK) and the lower-integral change of variables reduce to the compact set cK.
a.e.-strong measurability of ξ∘T: ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for c^{-n}H^n⌞M = T_#(H^n⌞M'), then compose with T.
Orientation: transfer the a.e. statement through the measurable embedding T and apply dilation invariance of approximate tangent planes (sibling tangent_space_dilation).

Null-set scaling, Lipschitz covering, compact-set integrability, strong measurability and orientation transfer are justified. The measurable embedding transfers arbitrary a.e. predicates correctly. Exactly the two declared child dependencies are used.
